label: copy-phase input k (fed-back k, from the 2nd copy input onward)
explanation: A token-identity feature for the fed-back letter k during the copy phase. It fires only when the input is k (100% of activation mass) and only in the copy phase (never on original-phase or delimiter k). It is essentially silent when the k is orig(0) fed back at the first copy step (recall_idx 1: 2 activations), and weaker when k is orig(1) (recall_idx 2: 8% of mass). Rate and magnitude peak at recall_idx 3-5. The strongest activations (up to 3.0) are on the first of a doubled k k in the middle of the sequence, and the second k of the pair is weaker. Activations are smaller on k near the end of the copy, for example the final input. About 27% of predicted steps stay inactive. These false positives are mostly k at recall_idx 2 or k on the last steps. Adding conditions to drop them (recall_idx>=3, to_go>=1) cuts recall more than it gains in precision. The feature does not fire on any other token.

issues: The test scores reproduce exactly: P 0.727, R 1.000, F1 0.842, mass recall 1.000. Only 1 activation in the test split is missed (k at recall_idx 1, 0.02 of max).
Token claim holds: in_tok k carries 100% of activation mass. No other in_tok ever fires.

Phase claim holds: there are 0 activations in the original and delimiter phases. All mass is in the copy phase. in_first==1 has 0 activations, consistent with the feature firing only on repeated (fed-back) k.
Recall_idx claims hold: recall_idx 1 has 2 activations in dev. recall_idx 2 holds 8.1% of mass and has precision 0.44. Mass peaks at recall_idx 3-5 (26%, 27%, 19%).
The doubled-k claim holds. In the top examples the first k of a 'k k' pair reaches 0.9-1.0 of max and the second k is at 0.3-0.6.

The 27% false positives are graded, not a sharp class. By subgroup: recall_idx==2 has precision 0.44, to_go==0 has 0.68, recall_idx>=6 has 0.70, to_go>=5 has 0.92, prev_tok a digit has 0.86. About 70% of the false positives are at recall_idx 2 or to_go 0, which matches the explanation.

Tightening does not help. recall_idx>=3 gives F1 0.837, below the original. Adding to_go<=6 changes nothing because to_go>=7 never occurs with recall_idx>=2. Within recall_idx 2 the dependence on L, prev_tok and out_tok is also graded (L<=4 0.67, L>=7 0.37), so no clean split improves on the original predicate.

Minor wording point: 'from the 2nd copy input onward' is accurate in that recall_idx>=2 means the fed-back token is orig(1) or later. Activations at recall_idx 2 are weak, so the label slightly overstates how consistently the feature fires there. This does not affect the verdict.
